text:
U.S. equities staged a sharp reversal on June 18, erasing the prior session's hawkish FOMC losses as the signed U.S.-Iran interim peace deal reopened the Strait of Hormuz and sent Brent crude lower. Tech led gains with Intel surging 9.9% on an Apple chip manufacturing deal, while the 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.45% in a bull-flattening move.

Bitcoin consolidated near $64,000–$64,500 as the broader crypto market found tentative support. The Fed's dual mandate remains the critical variable: the Bank of England held at 3.75% (7-2 vote), the SNB held at 0%, and the ECB's recent 25 bps hike to 2.25% illustrates the divergent global policy backdrop that complicates crypto's macro narrative.

With yields retreating and risk sentiment recovering, institutional digital asset flows face a critical test. A sustained DXY pullback from 100.3 highs and continued U.S.-Iran de-escalation would likely unlock the next BTC leg higher, but the Fed's hike probability in the dot plot remains the ceiling.
